The photographer shot his own kitchen on Long Island.

Industry observers note that douglas Friedman gives elaborate interiors a sense of drama, using natural light to bring out their materials. Along with photographing sumptuous rooms by Ken Fulk, Nicole Hollis, and Kelly Wearstler, the photographer has welcomed AD into his own Marfa retreat.

A modern retreat nestled in nature.

It has been revealed that alice Gao’s lens has been known to linger in shadows, resulting in a photograph that can romanticize even the most neutral, pared-back interiors. Her style brings minimalist, modern settings—such as those of clients Yabu Pushelberg and Toast UK, among others—beautifully to life.

This Brooklyn-based creative has brought an expert eye to shoots in countless stylish homes, restaurants like Altro Paradiso, and the studios of talents like Trueing and Christian Siriano.

The sunlit living room of a townhouse in Newly introduced York City’s West Village.

It has been revealed that his training as a painter informs Gaut’s portrait-like images of interiors, imbuing each space with personality. AD has published his images of Fresh York apartments, ski chalets in Wyoming, and farmhouses in Nova Scotia, but he’s also a fine art photographer whose prints have appeared in stores including Design Within Reach.

Inside celeb stylist Kate Young’s upstate Upcoming York home.

In a recent development, family life in all its facets is a frequent muse for William Geddes—his own wife and daughters included—though he’s also keen on assignments across the editorial, advertising, and publishing industries. A graduate of The New School, Parsons School for Design, Geddes also offers both simple and complex video shoots among his professional services.

A vignette from Elsa Perretti’s home in Spain.

Recent findings suggest that adrianna Glaviano finds visual wit in the smallest arrangements, such as jewelry on striped straws, or personal effects gathered around a sink. Her still-life sensibility offers designers a way to make the objects within a room part of its story. Working between Upcoming York and Milan, she counts AD France, HAY, FLOS, and Gohar World among her clients.

An Upstate New York couple painstakingly restored this geometric 1970s hideaway.

Golden hour appears to be Nick Glimenakis’s choice time to shoot, when he’s able to capture the warm light, long shadows, and exaggerated contrasts that up the drama in his imagery.

An indoor-outdoor space designed by Mike Moser Studio.

According to recent reports, residential design and hospitality meet in Christian Harder’s portfolio, which includes work with Jake Arnold, Ash, and AvroKO. His photographs of Darren Jett’s Brooklyn apartment for AD offer a useful introduction to his eye for rooms with personality. He’s also kept up a fine art photography practice and is repped by OneWay Gallery in Providence and Narragansett, Rhode Island.

In a Malibu home designed by Lala Reimagined, a dining area is filled with bentwood and natural fiber delights.

Ori Harpaz’s sharp editorial style has landed him multiple features in all of the top design magazines. His eye for color and penchant for strict angles mean his images are bold, striking, and arresting.

A marble bathroom in a Finger Lakes estate designed by Jeremiah Brent.

In a recent development, ethan Herrington’s career began in commercial still-life photography, and places and things get equal billing in his portfolio—welcome news for those who obsess over both the room and its contents. Based in Cold Spring, Fresh York, he has worked with Billy Cotton, Commune, and Studio Dorion.

A sunken living room oozes cool in this airy abode.

Industry observers note that formerly a fashion and textile print designer, Angela Hau—who operates out of San Francisco and NYC—has adapted her keen understanding of shape, scale, and balance to photography. Industry brands Thompson Street Studio, Egg Collective, and more have tapped Hau to beautifully capture interiors and product photography.

Studio Valle de Valle transformed a historic home in Toronto.

Jenni Kayne’s Los Angeles home and Neal Beckstedt’s wood-clad Chelsea apartment have both met Stephen Kent Johnson’s lens. He favors intimate views and revealing details over an all-encompassing wide angle, complete with soft light and carefully framed vignettes.

Inside a renovated California cabin with interiors designed by Fritz Haeg and Jeremy Schipper.

Sources indicate that recently relocated from LA, André Jones brings a sunny and warm approach to architecture and lifestyle photography. From rustic home interiors to sleek corporate buildings, his images are consistently well-framed and proportioned.

The living room in Walton Goggins’s home in Fresh York’s Hudson Valley.

The grand Victorian, simple Colonial, and traditional farmhouse-style homes scattered across upstate New York are a common subject for Kate Jordan’s lens. Her shots of Shaker-style kitchens and cozy living rooms depict all the warmth and familiarity they were designed to exude.

The city takes center stage in this Upcoming York apartment.

Long shadows and glimpses through windows give Joseph Kramm’s interiors a palpable sense of depth. His work with galleries including The Future Perfect and Hostler Burrows also makes him well versed in giving collectible furniture its moment.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most versatile interior photographers in the Northeast, Jared Kuzia captures residential projects up and down the Eastern Seaboard for architects, interior designers, and publications. Whether shooting urban apartments or coastal cabins, he is motivated by “conveying the essence of home,” as he puts it.

A bedroom in Isabella Rosselini’s converted barn on Long Island by architect Pietro Cicognani.

Francesco Lagnese’s interiors work moves comfortably between a spare, sunlit corner and the layered rooms of Tom Scheerer, Williams Lawrence, and Veere Grenney. Working between Upcoming York, Palm Beach, and all over Europe from his base in Munich, his itinerary extends well beyond the living room, as he also shoots architecture, portraits, and travel.

With an instantly recognizable, highly atmospheric style that’s won favor with top designers and stylists, William Jess Laird is consistently in high demand. His calm, minimal photos appear regularly in AD and many other leading art and design publications.

Olivia Palermo’s New York apartment.

Recent findings suggest that people are part of the picture in David Land’s photographs, from children playing in a living room to a family gathered on the sofa. In his images of work by Danielle Colding, Nina Barnieh-Blair, and more, color and everyday activity make these interiors feel welcoming, with life happening inside them.

A high-contrast interior captured by Heami Lee.

According to recent reports, there’s something innately playful about the images Lee captures for clients. Whether shooting still lifes for Edie Parker or Design Within Reach, Brooklyn-based Lee creates work that is undeniably cool.

Tour a Josh Greene–designed Upper East Side family home with a tented room.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

TESTING HIKING BOOTS, trail shoes, camping gear, and the like for a living means I spend a lot of time outdoors. Living in the Edwin B. Forsythe National Wildlife Refuge in coastal Upcoming Jersey, I’m fortunate to be able to step out my door and immediately be right in the middle of nature.

And when the weather starts to get colder, I take that as a cue not to head indoors, but to layer up. That means the hooded wetsuit goes on, an assortment of puffer jackets get put through the paces, and base layers become the first line of defense. With the holiday season upon us, here are six gifts that fellow nature lovers will find useful in the coming year. Better yet—they’re all available for purchase at Tractor Supply Co.

In a recent development, while Yeti’s coolers are certainly premium investments, the brand’s drinkware comprises some of its most accessible, hard-wearing products. Yes, the Yeti Rambler Water Bottle has been our best water bottle since it was released, but an insulated version is a must for anyone looking to stay outdoors. This 20-ounce stackable one is great because you can keep a few stacked in your camp kitchen gear and always know you’ve got mugs for the campsite.

Recent findings suggest that the Carhartt knit beanie has experienced a resurgence in popularity over the past couple winters, and for good reason: It’s affordable, it’s comfy in an acrylic knit, it comes in a ton of great colors, and it’s gonna last for years. While you really can’t go wrong with any color, I’m pretty partial to the traditional Carhartt brown, which evokes the iconic canvas Duck Jacket.

Recent findings suggest that my hands get pretty thrashed throughout the year surfing in the cold and constantly being outside, and the harsh, dry winter air is not very kind to them. I do my best with wearing gloves in the cold, but when I’m shooting photos of wildlife or practicing other hobbies that call for maximum dexterity, I sometimes fall short. That means I eventually get some cracked knuckles and need a repair balm like this aptly named option from Duke Cannon. It’s made with lanolin, which means it doesn’t leave my hands sticky or greasy like other lotions and balms tend to do.

Sources indicate that speaking of gloves, if I’m outside and not being super active (say, just walking the dog), or need to protect my hands while doing yardwork or bringing firewood into the house for the wood-burning stove, I turn to a leather pair like these. They tend to wear in, not out. And you can always just sport some cheapy knit gloves underneath if you want more insulation. Hearty gloves like this are always a must-have for campsite duty.

The nature preserve I live in is part of a pretty active salt-marsh tidal zone, and a creek runs behind my house that I launch my canoe and paddleboard from. This way of life requires me to be cognizant of (and really in tune with) the tides. It also requires a good pair of muck boots, because some days even just walking the dog means trekking through water. Deck boots (or those shorter ones that go just above the ankle) are pretty pointless in this sort of area—you really want something taller like these knee-highs, which are insulated and keep you dry all day long.

A thin (read: not puffy) vest is an overlooked layering option for the outdoors. It can function as an outer layer on warmer days, and when it cools off it still fits seamlessly under a shell or puffer. This reversible Field & Stream option is a solid choice because it’s water-resistant on one side and has soft polyester fleece on the other (adding even more insulation). And that cuffed neck is great for full coverage when it gets chilly.

According to recent reports, ryan Brower is the Senior Gear and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he tests the best products in outdoor gear, tech, running shoes, and more. He has written about the outdoors for nearly two decades and was previously the Managing Editor, Content Performance at Gear Patrol. He holds a B.A. in Sport Management and is a Certified Beer Server, having previously covered the craft beer industry. Ryan at the moment lives on the water in New Jersey with his wife and their dog.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner.
  • Six days after Nvidia’s board chair told investors “the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” the board voted unanimously to reinstate him as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.
  • Sources indicate that nvidia shares rose 33% to around $167, adding roughly a trillion dollars of market value in a session.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Six days after Nvidia’s board chair told investors “the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” the board voted unanimously to reinstate him as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.

Sources indicate that nvidia shares rose 33% to around $167, adding roughly a trillion dollars of market value in a session. Huang’s personal net worth climbed about $36.6 billion on his 3.5% stake, moving him to 13th on the Forbes global list. Short sellers took roughly $12.2 billion in paper losses, their worst single day since at least 2019, which wiped out the $10.5 billion they had booked the prior week.

The stock market absolutely ripped on the news. The Nasdaq closed up 6.51% at 24,089, its best day since April 2025. The S&P gained 4.7%, the Dow was +3%, and the VIX collapsed 25.8% to 26.62.

Industry observers note that bitcoin went along with the ride—for a few hours. It touched $63,929 intraday, up 5.1%, then spent the afternoon handing it back and finished near $61,000, barely up on the day. The ETFs used the pump to exit more, with BTC ETFs seeing another $570M in outflows on the day.

ETH and other majors also closed red. Alts gave back their gains. And the CMC top 20 index managed just 0.20% gain.

That’s a 19 to 1 ratio between what the Nasdaq captured and what Bitcoin kept, on the same catalyst, on the same day. Pain for the crypto bulls.

Recent findings suggest that what makes it even more painful, is that crypto fell with AI stocks the whole way down, and the standard explanation was that both trade on the same liquidity and the same risk appetite. Monday tested that and the correlation fell through. The AI trade got a catalyst and markets bounced. Crypto didn’t bounce with it.

In a recent development, as for Nvidia’s reversal decision itself, questions remain to say the least. The board says it was satisfied with Huang’s “candor and ability to lead,” and that input from senior U.S. officials left it confident his return “poses no national security risk.” Trump publicly pushed for it and said the board had sought assurance on the espionage allegations. What actually changed between November 17 and November 23 hasn’t been explained. The independent directors’ investigation is still open, and Nvidia is now standing up a board committee for national security and export-control oversight plus recruiting a chief compliance officer.

Perhaps answers will trickle out over time. The AI trade may not need them anyway. And crypto, well, it's in its own world right now, waiting for its own catalysts (likely quantum-related). But it’s very unclear that catalyst is coming in 2026, and it’s becoming clear that many are not interested in waiting for the answers….

Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on the SSP

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.
  • As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.
  • The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer stated in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer announced earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

Production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the latest i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen remarked in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The firm also said investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”.

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW noted several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

According to recent reports, however, the Audi A4 E-tron delay is not entirely about software. The Autocar report claims Audi demanded significant changes to the SSP platform for the A4 E-tron so it more closely matched the current gas version.

Audi reportedly wanted individual footwells for front and rear passengers, which would require repositioning the battery.

The luxury brand also reportedly asked for a 48V electrical system instead of the traditional 12V setup initially planned.

While development of the Golf EV is on hold, VW’s works council noted the pause will not delay its launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030. The Audi A4 E-tron is now expected to arrive around 2029.

The 5 Best Smart Rings, Tested by Fitness Editors

📅 31 Jan 2023 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved.
  • SMART RINGS HAVE quickly become one of the most popular forms of health tracking on the market today.
  • Recent findings suggest that one thing to be clear on: Smart rings and fitness trackers are not created equal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SMART RINGS HAVE quickly become one of the most popular forms of health tracking on the market today. These minimalist wearables deliver advanced health and fitness metrics—like sleep, recovery, readiness, and even stress tracking—without the bulk of a watch or the distraction of a screen. We put the most popular models through weeks of testing and spoke with experts to find the best smart rings for every kind of user.

Recent findings suggest that one thing to be clear on: Smart rings and fitness trackers are not created equal. Smart rings definitely focus more on overall wellness while fitness trackers are more for dialing in on workout metrics. While smart rings still offer workout modes and step tracking, the workout metrics are not nearly as in-depth as those you’ll find on an Apple Watch or Garmin. But these devices offer a way to monitor your daily health-related metrics in a more subtle and discreet way. Whether you’re looking to track your sleep more accurately, understand your recovery needs, or monitor other daily health-related metrics, there’s a smart ring for you on this list.

It has been revealed that as the Fitness and Reviews editor at Men’s Health, it’s my job to test the latest and greatest fitness tech, including smart rings. I’ve been a smart ring wearer since the first Oura Ring was released, and they’ve been an key tool in providing me with health data throughout the years.

In order to build this guide of the best smart rings, I gathered the most popular model of each brand on the market and tried them out for at least two weeks. I wore them during workouts, walks, writing, sleep, and ordinary errands around the home and out and about. This guide is the result of our experience and testing, and will be updated as newly introduced products are released.

Here is our guide to the best smart rings.

The Oura Ring continues to come out on top for us, even as we continue to test newly introduced more rings over the years. As the most up-to-date version of Oura’s popular smart ring, the Oura Ring 5 brings new sensors and algorithmic improvements to an already powerful health-tracking device. This version nixed the tangible sensors and cut back on the thickness to build an even sleeker, thinner, and more comfortable model—but don’t worry, the data has only improved with each iteration.

Sources indicate that from a health-tracking standpoint, the Oura Ring 5 gives you a holistic picture of your wellness: temperature variation, sleep analysis, blood oxygen monitoring, heart rate variability (HRV), resting heart rate, activity tracking, and daytime stress detection. If you wear it overnight, it automatically logs how long and how well you slept, how much time you spent in deep sleep, REM, and light sleep, and even gives you a readiness score each morning.

I personally love the sleep-tracking feature on my Oura Ring. It’s definitely my most-utilized function—it’s the first thing I check every morning when I wake up. And I have to say, it’s highly accurate. I wake up at least once a night, and I’ll typically look at the clock when I do. When I check my Oura sleep metrics in the morning, it demonstrates my midnight wake-up time almost exactly every time.

Read More: Our Hands-On Review of the Oura Ring 5.

Recent findings suggest that for those who want insights into sleep, heart rate, and recovery—without dropping $400 or signing up for a monthly membership—the RingConn Gen 2 Air offers great value. RingConn has refined its hardware with this second generation, offering a noticeably lighter and more comfortable fit than the original.

It has been revealed that what makes RingConn different is its inclusion of sleep apnea detection, a rare find in this industry, especially without requiring a subscription. However, the Air does not offer this feature that RingConn is known for. The RingConn Gen 2 Air monitors a wide range of sleep metrics, including time spent in each sleep stage, movement during the night, and breathing irregularities. It’s an ideal ring for anyone trying to better understand how their overnight recovery impacts daily energy and long-term health, but it does not monitor sleep apnea like its sister product, the RingConn Gen 2.

I do have some qualms with the workout tracking. While those looking for in-depth fitness tracking are more likely to go with something like a Garmin or Whoop, the RingConn Gen 2 Air is especially basic when it comes to distinguishing different workouts. I wouldn’t really trust it to correctly judge what kind of workout I’m doing, but perhaps running. It can log activity and heart rate zones, but its technology for exercise auto-detection is new this year and not entirely accurate yet.

In a recent development, still, for people more concerned with sleep and recovery than fitness performance, the Gen 2 Air is more than capable. Just note that sizes run slightly large, so it’s worth using their sizing kit or sizing down if you’re between sizes. The company also released an updated version, the Gen 3 Air, but honestly, it’s more expensive, heavier, and still can’t compete with the Oura Ring. So better to stick with this version in my opinion.

Read More: Best Fitness Trackers.

According to recent reports, samsung’s long-awaited Galaxy Ring is a newer addition to the smart ring catalog. Crafted from lightweight titanium and available in three finishes, if you already use a Samsung Galaxy phone or smartwatch the integration takes no effort.

Recent findings suggest that designed to work seamlessly with Samsung Health, the Galaxy Ring tracks heart rate, activity, and sleep highly accurately. Its biggest selling point may be its emphasis on stress and sleep metrics, which have become central to Samsung’s wellness strategy. Galaxy Ring will even give you a sleep animal that reflects your sleep habits—dog is the golden ticket there. If you get, say, a turtle (you fall asleep slowly and may have some interruptions throughout the night), Galaxy AI will bring you a proposed proposal of action to get your sleep back on track, taking sleep tracking to that next level. It also includes skin temperature sensors and supports auto workout detection for some activities, like walking and running.

Industry observers note that while it lacks compatibility with iPhones, it does everything Android customers need it to. And although Samsung hasn’t introduced a subscription strategy yet, there’s speculation that one may arrive in the future to access advanced features. For now, all features are free, making it one of the most robust and cost-effective options for Android users. And if you’re debating between the Oura Ring and the Samsung Galaxy Ring, we have things to say.

Amazfit is known for its budget-friendly fitness tech that often outperforms what you may expect from an Amazon brand product. The fresh Helio Ring continues that by offering a smart ring that boasts solid metrics, sleek design, and no subscription fee. It’s especially alluring for people already in the Amazfit ecosystem—this ring pairs seamlessly with devices like the T-Rex 3.

The Helio Ring includes the basic smart ring metrics: sleep tracking, readiness scoring, heart rate monitoring, and activity logging. It also offers a few innovative features, like built-in AI coaching, which can help you adjust your sleep habits, activity levels, and even recovery tips based on your daily data. The ring is comfortable and well-made, featuring a durable titanium exterior and a fairly slim profile.

That noted, if you’re expecting Oura-level insights, you may find the data a little surface-level. It doesn’t really stack up to its competition when it comes to the app and the data. I would say it’s much more of a smart ring for beginners looking to save a few hundred dollars while getting something that is generally useful and looks good on the finger. To go a little deeper, the app is functional, though not especially polished, and some might miss the granularity offered by more premium competitors. Still, for the price—just under $200—the Helio Ring offers a step into smart rings, especially for anyone prioritizing affordability and comfort.

The first time I put on the Oura Ring 4, I figured that this was as good as it got when it comes to smart rings. Super low profile. Super light. And a charge that lasts for a week. The removal of the nodes in previous generations was the clincher.

Recent findings suggest that the app and software that come with an Oura Ring come with any of the versions. I am impressed by how small and thin the Oura Ring 5 is. They’ve managed to put that impressive tech into a smaller unit, which is even more discreet. But personally, I find the ring too small, to the point that it feels a little strange and less secure on my finger.

It has been revealed that senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM, still prefers the slim design of the Oura Ring 5, but if you want to score almost all of the same features in a bigger ring, you might want to opt for the Ring 4. You might even score a serious discount, as their last-gen model goes on sale often.

Read More: Our Hands-On Review of the Oura Ring 4.

The Ultrahuman Ring AIR was previously on this list as our Best No-Membership-Needed Smart Ring, but after a legal dispute with another smart ring maker, they could no longer sell that version in the United States.

We are presently testing a review unit of the Ultrahuman Ring Pro, the brand’s latest offering, which is currently available for pre-order, to see if it’s worth adding to this guide. Ultrahuman is promising a longer battery life, advanced insights, and a more streamlined app experience.

In a recent development, design is more than just looks—it’s about wearability. Smart rings need to be lightweight enough for 24/7 wear, durable enough for workouts and showers, and comfortable enough that you forget they’re on. Most are made from lightweight metals like titanium or aluminum alloy, and many brands include a sizing kit to find your ideal size. Pay attention to internal sensor placement as well—rings with smooth, node-free interiors are more comfortable for long-term use.

Color and style also matter. While many smart rings come in simple black or silver, several brands offer gold, matte gray, or brushed finishes to suit different tastes (though those options can cost more). Just remember: These rings are not meant to be the flashiest piece of jewelry you wear—they are designed for functionality, and you will notice scratches over time, regardless of the color you choose.

It has been revealed that the finger that you place your smart ring on also matters. While a smart ring can still work no matter what finger you place it on, most companies recommend that you place it on your forefinger on your non-dominant hand, because that is where your pulse is the strongest and is less likely to get in the way of daily tasks.

In a recent development, the ring’s hardware is only half the equation—the app experience is where you’ll glean all the information your ring has to offer. Some apps, like Oura and Samsung Health, offer intuitive scoring systems for recovery, readiness, and sleep, plus easy-to-read graphics and insights. Others, like Ultrahuman and Amazfit, may have a steeper learning curve because the interface isn't laid out as intuitively. However, they aren’t outrageously difficult to follow, just a little less categorized than others like Oura and Samsung.

Sources indicate that you’ll also want to consider whether the app integrates with your other health platforms, like Apple Health, Google Fit, or Garmin Connect—and whether it provides usable insights, not just raw data. For example, you don’t just want to see a low readiness score—you want to hear from your ring why that score may be too low and how to fix it: "Your activity was through the roof yesterday, maybe take it easy today and find some time to recover." The best apps break down complex biometrics into simple takeaways you can actually use.

According to recent reports, in all our testing with smart rings (and even fitness trackers in general), accuracy has been the hardest metric to measure. For these smart rings, we found that bigger names like Oura and Galaxy Ring had the most consistent results across sleep stages, heart rate, HRV, and temperature tracking. Which makes sense with more funding backing the brand names. We also compared their workout metrics against wrist trackers like the Apple Watch, and accuracy held up for most workouts. Ultrahuman was close behind, especially succeeding in the recovery category. RingConn and Amazfit sometimes showed small accuracy inconsistencies, especially with workout differentiation. If you look at the prices here, you’ll see a pattern: The more expensive the ring, the more accurate the data.

Industry observers note that these rings aren't meant to give you the most accurate workout training data, though. If you're looking for a device to wear only for your workout, that will provide you with training insights, you are going to want to go for a fitness tracker designed for that situation. If you are going to wear it during your runs or lifts, you may want a wrist or torso tracker. "Nobody really needs to be wearing two fitness trackers at any time," claims Men's Health Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. "Find the one that fits your needs and will give you the best data for your goals.".

In a recent development, smart rings aren’t medical devices. They offer estimates based on algorithms and sensor data, not lab-verified testing. But if you use them consistently, even numbers that aren’t quite perfect can give you valuable insight into your health patterns over time, as rings will compare your past data against your current data for a more complete picture.

As with most technology, the more you use the product, the more often you have to charge it. Typically, a fully charged smart ring lasts about four to eight days. Oura and RingConn top the list with a full week of use per charge (potentially eight days with light use). Samsung’s Galaxy Ring is also impressive with around seven days. However, less expensive rings generally run closer to four or five days of charge.

Recent findings suggest that most rings charge via a small dock or case, and a full charge takes about 60 to 90-minutes. Consider how the charging process fits into your routine—especially if you plan to wear the ring to sleep. A good time to charge is often in the shower each day (and it's also a good time to clean it). With this method, you’ll never have to leave the ring off for that extended 90 minute charge time. And frankly, you won’t even have to worry about the length of time your ring will hold a charge. I do this with my ring, and I’ve never dipped below a 70% charge (except that one time I forgot my charger on a week-long vacation, oops).

Sources indicate that well, that all depends on your individual priorities. Smartwatches generally offer more features: GPS, message notifications, guided workouts, music controls, and in-depth workout analytics. But they also tend to be bulkier, need more frequent charging, and cause screen distractions.

Sources indicate that smart rings, on the other hand, are streamlined, screenless, and usually focused on sleep, stress, recovery, and wellness in general. They’re ideal if you want to track biometrics without getting sucked into a screen every few minutes. For the data-obsessed, wearing a smart ring at night and adding a smartwatch during the day is a great combination.

That mentioned, if you’re a serious runner, cyclist, or athlete who wants workout coaching and performance stats in real time, a smartwatch is likely a better fit. If you’re focused on recovery, sleep quality, and managing stress, a smart ring may be the choice for you.

Its lightweight titanium build and water resistance make it comfortable for 24/7 wear, and the battery reliably lasts up to a week on a single charge. The Oura Ring 4 excels in sleep tracking, heart rate variability monitoring, and daily readiness scoring, with an intuitive app that presents data in a clear, actionable format. For most owners, the Ring 4 delivers a seamless, unobtrusive way to monitor overall wellness, making it a favorite among those who dislike wrist-worn trackers.

Charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. Following an early life in athletics, Charles became a NASM-certified trainer and began writing programs alongside the most respected coaches in the world. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.
  • We knew it was coming soon after the latest model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that BYD opened pre-orders for the third-generation Tang starting at about $34,000 in China. This five-seat flagship SUV packs more than you’d expect for the money, with two massive 30-inch-plus screens inside and up to 850 km (528 miles) of CLTC range.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the latest model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD announced on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

In a recent development, inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD remarked.

Like many of its upcoming flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division stated third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it launched in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

According to recent reports, the Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

Will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

Volkswagen may have just hinted at the name of its next affordable EV

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen is getting ready to launch a latest electric car starting at about €20,000 ($22,000) in 2027, and it looks like the entry-level EV may no longer be nameless.
  • In a recent development, the new entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer stated last March after unveiling the ID.
  • Volkswagen said the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen is getting ready to launch a latest electric car starting at about €20,000 ($22,000) in 2027, and it looks like the entry-level EV may no longer be nameless. A newly filed trademark could have just given away what VW aims to call it.

In a recent development, the new entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer stated last March after unveiling the ID. EVERY1 concept car.

Volkswagen said the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).

Industry observers note that the new model will sit below the ID. Polo in Volkswagen’s Electric Urban Car Family, a lineup of compact, affordable electric cars.

Volkswagen’s current entry-level EV lineup includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, the Cupra Raval, and Skoda Epiq, all based on its latest MEB+ platform.

After launching the lower-priced standard versions of the ID. Polo and ID. Cross recently, starting at €24,995 and €27,995, respectively, Volkswagen is preparing to launch an even smaller, more affordable EV next year.

A recent trademark filing with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the German DPMA may have just revealed the name of VW’s upcoming €20,000 EV.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen filed a trademark application for the name ID. UP on October 22, 2026, with the EUIPO and DPMA, suggesting this will be the name of the upcoming electric car in 2027.

The trademark follows previous reports that VW planned to revive the former Up! name as part of its shift away from its previous numerical naming scheme (ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, etc.).

Volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.

According to recent reports, the VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.

Sources indicate that volkswagen remarked it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).

Sources indicate that the production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine fresh models VW intends to launch by 2027.

Volkswagen previously said the entry-level EV will be 3,880 mm long, which would position it between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and the ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.

The VW Group’s newly introduced Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.

All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.

Volkswagen noted the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal, software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which it is developing through its joint venture with Rivian.

Ah, finally a car in the upper range of being meaningful and sensible.

If someone needs more, then those are obviously special needs people. Being like can't enter and exit such a sensible car. Or like having to move the 15 horses of their 5 daughters. Or being a fieldworker driving a gazillion miles every day. Or requiring a lot of attention from lesser beings.

In March, the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies (RV Tech) joint venture tested the fresh SDV architecture on the ID. EVERY1, alongside Audi and Scout reference vehicles, validating over-the-air (OTA) capabilities.

The upcoming architecture will enable “highly automated driving features” and “advanced infotainment solutions,” with continuous OTA updates.

While VW stated it will deploy the SDV architecture in “electric vehicles across markets in the Western Hemisphere,” the entry-level EV is not expected to reach the States.

Volkswagen is, however, preparing to launch the ID. Tiguan, which will launch in 2027 as the successor to the ID.4 (and ID.5 in Europe).

#178605. Tech Report: The Kids Are Outside: The Rise of the Adult Children’s ADU

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (976 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Architecturaldigest ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The Kids Are Outside: The Rise of the Adult Children’s ADU

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that when Diane and Steve Weaver of Castro Valley, California, shipped their son Sam off to college in 2013, they hoped he’d someday find his dream job and a nice home.
  • While in-law suites and granny flats (a nickname for when ADUs house in-laws) have become popular among young, successful homeowners who want their elderly parents nearby, a growing number of Americans are now adding ADUs to their properties to house adult children threatening to move back in and reverse their status as empty nesters.
  • Blame the return of the flock on the home affordability crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that when Diane and Steve Weaver of Castro Valley, California, shipped their son Sam off to college in 2013, they hoped he’d someday find his dream job and a nice home. And while Sam is thriving professionally as a sales rep with his own place, they never expected that his house would be in their backyard. But the nightmarish Bay Area real estate market made a 400-square-foot ADU (accessory dwelling unit) on his parents’ property, complete with a separate entrance and direct street access, seem like the best option for the 32-year-old. “It was becoming difficult for him to afford rent while also saving toward eventually buying a place of his own,” Diane tells AD. “He’s close by, but it really feels like he has his own home.”.

While in-law suites and granny flats (a nickname for when ADUs house in-laws) have become popular among young, successful homeowners who want their elderly parents nearby, a growing number of Americans are now adding ADUs to their properties to house adult children threatening to move back in and reverse their status as empty nesters.

Diane and Steve Weaver on their property’s ADU.

Blame the return of the flock on the home affordability crisis. These days a homebuyer needs an annual income between $110,000 and $113,000—well above the national average income of $64,220 per year—to comfortably afford a median-priced home in the US, which is currently priced at $434,900. While this has led some grown kids to move back into their childhood bedrooms, in cases where acreage allows, families like the Weavers are opting to be neighbors instead of housemates by setting up self-contained living spaces on the same lot as their single-family homes. In California, they’re certainly no outlier. The state has passed legislation specifically encouraging the construction of ADUs to address the housing shortage—which resulted in quadruple the number of ADU permits issued in the Golden State from 2017 to 2022.

Those in the ADU construction game say families like the Weavers make up an increasingly large slice of their business. Jeremy Nova, co-founder of the Colorado-based prefab ADU builder Studio Home, indicates ADUs for adult children are popular among his clients because the arrangement is mutually beneficial. The kids are afforded some independence and the ability to save money, “while for the parents, it can also be a long-term investment. The same space that houses an adult child today could eventually become a rental or a separate living space for a caregiver.” ADU builders on the opposite coast are seeing the same demand. Justin Olewack, president of Bolt Builders, says that ADUs for adult children are becoming a top request among his clientele in the DC, Virginia, and Maryland areas, where housing costs have risen 61 percent since 2016.

If it cuts costs and results in a sellable amenity down the line, perhaps moving back home isn’t the failure-to-launch scenario it was once seen as.

An ADU by Studio Home, built in the backyard of a Scottsdale, Arizona, family’s property.

Once a family’s adult child moves out of the property’s ADU, especially if it has a kitchen and bathroom, the structure can serve as a rental, providing passive income for retired parents. Tracy Noh, who hired John Brennan of BZBuild Co to build her daughter Eliza Bowen an ADU in Burbank, was thinking long-term with her compound planning. “An in-home apartment would require sharing the space of our 1,000-square-foot main home. And, as someone who works from home, the ADU seemed a better solution,” she states.

Noh and Eliza show off their Burbank ADU.

According to recent reports, the living arrangement has also enabled Noh and her daughter to develop their own life paths. The structure gives her daughter a space in which she can become a young adult, and Noh the opportunity to step back from making the day-to-day household decisions. The former is learning how to manage her own household: planning meals, budgeting expenses, and making time for household chores.

“That change in dynamic also allows us both to remain much calmer in our interactions with each other,” Noh claims. It’s not just because there’s a separate place for each of them to retreat to; Noh says she has “gained an enormous amount of respect for Eliza and her ability to manage her own home. It’s a fabulous opportunity to begin to build that adult-to-adult relationship with your child.”.

The interior of Tracy Noh’s ADU by BZBuild Co.

While modest ADUs serve single occupants just fine, more sizable ADUs allow a family’s adult children to bring their own kids in tow. Oren Amir, co-founder of SoCal builder GO Home Builders, points out that in his experience, the catalyst for aging parents to build an ADU for their adult children is almost never just the adult child themselves: It’s the grandchild they will be bringing with them. “The call comes a few months before or after a baby arrives,” he states. The grandparents don’t want to travel to visit their grandkids; they want them living nearby. Rent in Los Angeles is what stops people from saving, and early parenthood is when saving matters most, Amir says. An ADU in a grandparent’s backyard, therefore, lets the adult children stay in the neighborhood, raise the baby near help, and set some money aside for when the time comes to leave the nest for good. “Everyone gets what they need and nobody has to move in,” Amir says of the arrangement.

While the Weaver family ADU is Sam’s for now, it could grow up to be a granny flat someday. “It’s possible that Sam might live in the main house and we could move into the ADU as we age,” indicates Diane. “It gives us a lot of options for how the space can be used as our family’s needs change.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rinnai has introduced a fresh lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.

According to recent reports, the REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes. It builds on Rinnai’s existing REHP lineup, with changes designed to make the units easier to install, monitor, and maintain.

According to recent reports, heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank. Moving that heat requires less electricity than producing it with conventional electric resistance elements. There’s no fuel combustion at the appliance, although emissions from its electricity supply depend on the grid.

Rinnai lists a Uniform Energy Factor, or UEF, of 3.75 for the 50-gallon model and 4.0 for the two larger versions. Higher numbers mean greater efficiency under standardized testing; actual bills depend on electricity rates, hot water use, and installation conditions.

It has been revealed that the lineup delivers up to 91 gallons of hot water in the first hour, depending on tank size. That rating includes both stored hot water and what the unit can heat during that hour – useful context when several people take consecutive showers.

It has been revealed that there are five operating modes, 4.5 kW backup heating elements, and a variable-speed fan designed to keep noise down. The heat pump can operate with ambient air as low as 37°F.

Installation is where some of the more practical upgrades show up.

In a recent development, the new Rinnai heat pump water heater units have water connections on both the top and side, giving installers more options for connecting existing plumbing. Both the air intake and exhaust are on top, allowing zero side clearance where Rinnai’s installation requirements permit.

An optional ducting kit adds flexibility for tighter spaces. Carrying handles help with moving the tank into place, and the air filter slides out horizontally from the side for cleaning.

Rinnai has also added a third tank temperature sensor to the 50- and 80-gallon models to help manage hot water delivery.

It has been revealed that wifi adds remote monitoring and control. Rinnai’s updated Central app supports the REHPW series, including scheduling and tools to use time-of-use electricity rates to manage energy use.

The units also carry CTA-2045 AC Level 2 certification for demand response. That gives compatible utility programs a way to communicate with the water heater and adjust its electricity use. Rinnai says the certification can help qualify homeowners for local and state utility demand-response rebates; availability depends on the program.

The series is Energy Star certified, meets NEEA Tier 4 requirements, and complies with California’s Title 24 requirements, including JA13, according to Rinnai. Warranty coverage includes 10 years for the tank and other parts, plus one year for labor.

According to recent reports, I’m very happy with my hybrid heat pump water heater. I run it in heat pump only mode in summer and it helps cool the house for free. For anyone on the fence, especially your utility offers a rebate, it’s definitely worth looking at.

Rinnai directs buyers to an installer for pricing, so the upfront cost – and how much a local rebate might offset it – will require a quote. However, the REHP series price on Amazon hovers around the $2,000 mark.

#178596. ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Inside the Psychedelic 1970s-Inspired Dystopian Sets

‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Inside the Psychedelic 1970s-Inspired Dystopian Sets

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that francis Lawrence, director of The Hunger Games, has a tradition with author Suzanne Collins.
  • According to recent reports, lawrence’s latest adaptation, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (in theaters today), returns to Panem, a postapocalyptic nation where the ruling Capitol controls twelve districts through extreme systemic oppression—most notoriously the titular spectacle in which children are selected by lottery and forced to fight to the death in an arena.
  • District 12’s female tribute Maysilee Donner (McKenna Grace) at the reaping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that francis Lawrence, director of The Hunger Games, has a tradition with author Suzanne Collins. Before bringing a new installment of her bestselling dystopian saga to the significant screen, the two join forces to envision how the fictional world of Panem will take shape. “I go to New York each time, and we sit in a conference room at Scholastic,” states Lawrence, who has directed five of the franchise’s six films. “We go through the book page by page and beat out what we think the movie is going to look like.”.

According to recent reports, lawrence’s latest adaptation, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (in theaters today), returns to Panem, a postapocalyptic nation where the ruling Capitol controls twelve districts through extreme systemic oppression—most notoriously the titular spectacle in which children are selected by lottery and forced to fight to the death in an arena. Set twenty-four years before the original The Hunger Games (2012) plotline, the prequel follows District 12’s sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada)—the future mentor (played by Woody Harrelson) to Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson)—as he is selected to fight in the Second Quarter Quell, a particularly sadistic rendition of the Games held every twenty-five years.

District 12’s female tribute Maysilee Donner (McKenna Grace) at the reaping.

According to recent reports, though the dystopia is set in a future North America, the previous prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (2023), drew from the architecture of 1940s and ’50s postwar Berlin to depict evil President Snow’s rise to tyranny. Set forty years later, Sunrise explores Panem at a new stage of its evolution. Designed by returning production designer Uli Hanisch, the film follows Haymitch from his impoverished mining district, which barely evolves throughout the series’s sixty-five year timeline, to the opulent Capitol, whose extravagance is expressed through a 1970s-inflected visual lexicon.

Industry observers note that “I realized the ’70s fall right smack in the middle between that movie and the originals, so we could lean into that,” says Lawrence. Hanisch and his team incorporated references to Andy Warhol, Studio 54, and the decade’s psychedelic color palette, appropriating its progressive spirit to convey the Capitol’s opulence and authoritarianism—and, particularly in the arena, using the aesthetic as a means of deception. “To turn the ’70s style from something progressive, liberal, young, and open-minded into something evil is a twist,” says Hanisch. “But that is the key to the entire film’s design.”.

Haymitch and Maysilee as allies in the arena. The forest portion was filmed separately near Cologne, Germany.

Sources indicate that the stylistic choice is also a poignant nod to Collins’s original inspiration for the book series. The 1970s marked a transformation in American television: as color TVs became ubiquitous in households across the country, sporting spectacles, variety demonstrates, and beauty pageants flourished, establishing cultural touchstones that would help shape the contemporary reality programming Collins critiques and satirizes in The Hunger Games. “I was flipping through the channels one night between reality television programs and actual footage of the Iraq War, when the idea came to me,” Collins recalled in a 2018 interview with The Fresh York Times. The juxtaposition inspired her to explore just-war theory for young people through an authoritarian dystopia in which mass entertainment is an instrument of political control.

From an abandoned rural steel mill to authoritarian monuments from postwar Berlin, the film draws on politically charged German sites to capture Panem at a pivotal stage in its political and architectural evolution.

Production Designer Uli Hanisch at the District 12 set. “District 12 is the most sentimental set to me because I’d known this site near my hometown my entire life,” Hanisch notes.

Industry observers note that to recreate the Appalachian-inspired, deteriorating industrial landscape of District 12 that was shot in Atlanta in the original series, the production utilized a sprawling abandoned steel mill in Duisburg, Germany, Hanisch’s hometown. “I wish we had it in the original movies, because it is an unbelievable space,” Lawrence states of the post-industrial, rural landscape, which also appeared in The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, Hanisch’s first film in the franchise. “Everywhere you look is exactly how I have always imagined District 12.”.

Recent findings suggest that while District 12 was filmed near Atlanta in the original films, director Francis Lawrence’s fascination with German architecture brought production to Berlin for The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. It was there that he began collaborating with Berlin-based production designer Hanisch, who proposed this steel mill nearby his hometown for the latest location. Upon seeing photographs, Lawrence exclaimed, “Are you kidding me? ... Let’s go tomorrow,” and promptly flew out to see it for himself.

The production designer added modest huts at the edge of a nearby quarry to recreate the Seam, home to Haymitch, his girlfriend Lenore Dove (Whitney Peak), and fellow tribute Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), its humble dwellings contrasting the more prosperous merchant district inhabited by fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace).

“Unlike the Capitol, District 12 doesn't evolve stylistically throughout the films. Nobody is investing in it, and everything is gradually deteriorating,” Hanisch explains. The vivid purples and oranges of the Capitol’s ‘70s palette are notably absent, only appearing prominently in propaganda decorating the reaping square, including Hunger Games campaign materials and posters portraying Snow as Panem’s number-one Peacekeeper.

Druscilla in the Capitol before the tribute interviews, which is broadcast to all of Panem.

In the Capitol, however, the architecture takes on a distinctly ‘70s flair. Rooted in the Roman concept of panem et circenses, or “bread and circuses,” from which Panem takes its name, the architecture reinforces the government’s manipulation through spectacle. In the background is Berlin's International Congress Centrum, a colossal, aluminum-clad convention center that opened in 1979, which Lawrence describes as “Cold War-era Berlin showing off in a modern way.” As West Berlin’s most expensive postwar building, the futuristic complex was publicly subsidised to showcase economic prosperity and technological advancement—an evocative backdrop for the Capitol’s own display of authoritarianism.

“It’s a time of peace for the Capitol with no rebel attacks, so Snow's had time to build the city up in a way that is an extravagant show of power,” Lawrence explains. The chariot parade, which introduces the tributes before the Games, similarly unfolds against the historically-charged Berlin Olympiastadion, which was designed by Werner March for the 1936 Olympics under Nazi Germany to project state power and an illusion of timeless permanence.

Industry observers note that the upstairs library in Plutarch’s home, which he inherited from the Heavensbee dynasty. Reflecting the Capitol’s classic style, it contrasts the Plutarch’s modern downstairs salon which features Warhol-inspired portraits, including one of director Lawrence.

Sources indicate that the Capitol's grandeur is also exhibited inside the mansion of Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons), a cameraman with historic ties to Panem’s ruling class. “This was one of my favorite sets because of the scope and scale” Lawrence claims, noting how its excess reflects the dynasty's immense wealth. Filmed at Berlin's late-1960s modernist Congress Center, the circular residence required twenty-five vans of retro-modern furniture to fill it. The salon, decked in vibrant 1970s furnishings and Warhol-inspired art, showcases Plutarch's modern sensibilities, in stark contrast to the upstairs library inherited from his family. “We wanted to distinguish Plutarch from the dynasty he comes from,” Lawrence explains, reflecting on how the expansive volumes must be a facade of intellectual sophistication.

The set decoration department spent weeks hand-folding and assembling thousands of hollow cardboard books, interspersed with real volumes, including a collection of Edgar Allan Poe’s poetry, which Plutarch references to Haymitch. “We imagined Plutarch might actually be the first Heavensbee to read some of those books,” Hanisch says. “He even says the library is one of the few worthwhile things his ancestors accomplished.”.

Industry observers note that the library's custom-built curved bookshelves envelope the characters, symbolising the insularity of Capitol society. “Circles represent both inclusion and exclusion,” Hanisch says. “If you are in the circle, you're in. And if you're not, you're out.” As fans of the franchise will know, Plutarch (originally played by Philip Seymour Hoffman) later reveals himself as a double agent and leader of the underground rebellion against Snow’s regime.

Recent findings suggest that the aspect ratio expands as Haymitch ascends into the eye-shaped arena, emphasizing the landscape’s immersive scale and beauty. While scouting locations, Lawrence drew inspiration from the dramatic landscapes in Terrence Malick’s A Hidden Life. “I had that in my head, only it was a little trippier. The Asturias were perfect,” he recalls. The kaleidoscopic design also inspired the official logo of the 50th Hunger Games, extending the arena’s psychedelic imagery into the Capitol’s propaganda.

It has been revealed that the Quarter Quell arena, in particular, embodies the surreal, fantastical ethos of the 1970s that permeates the film, illustrating how the Capitol exploits beauty to disguise its underlying manipulation and brutality. “As I was reading with Suzanne, I mentioned there was an Alice in Wonderland-like element to it, which made me think of the song ‘White Rabbit,’ which made me think of the late ’60s, early ’70s,” Lawrence recalls. “That kind of broke something open for me.”.

Designed in the shape of an eye, the eight to ten mile arena serves as a metaphor for the Capitol's omnipresent surveillance. A golden Cornucopia forms its pupil; vibrant meadows its iris; and the surrounding mountain ranges its whites. In the book, Haymitch describes the especially lethal arena masquerading as an idyllic landscape as a “poisonous beauty of an arena.”.

In a recent development, lawrence and Haymitch in the arena. The physical flowers were concentrated in the foreground, while visual effects extended the colorful landscape into the distance.

Recent findings suggest that seeking to capture as much natural landscape as possible, Hanisch and location manager Klaus große Darrelmann discovered a remote valley in Asturias, Spain, surrounded by the Cantabrian Mountains. Transforming the isolated valley into a psychedelic paradise proved an enormous undertaking.“The arena was our nemesis,” indicates Hanisch, recalling how the production had to bring extensive resources to the remote terrain. “You can't even imagine how far away it was or how hard it was to get to.” Crews spent weeks individually installing hundreds of thousands of artificial flowers throughout the meadows and forests.

It has been revealed that despite the arena’s dreamlike beauty, water sources, flowers, and vegetation conceal deadly poisons. “It’s the most colorful and playful dystopia you’ll ever see,” producer Nina Jacobson notes. Perhaps more than anywhere else in Panem, the arena encapsulates how the Capitol weaponizes the electric zeitgeist of the ‘70s as an instrument of control. “To have something so overwhelmingly beautiful and seductive but poisonous and deadly is very cruel,” Hanisch says. “That contradiction captures the mentality of Panem at this point in its history.”.

#178590. Latest Update: Should You Let Your Teen Play Grand Theft Auto?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (986 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Should You Let Your Teen Play Grand Theft Auto?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (986 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As parents, what should you and your kids consider before picking up that controller?
  • With the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, caregivers may soon find themselves negotiating with teens who insist that everyone they know is playing it.
  • “I know the difference between real life and video games.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

As parents, what should you and your kids consider before picking up that controller?

With the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, caregivers may soon find themselves negotiating with teens who insist that everyone they know is playing it.

“I know the difference between real life and video games.”.

And, of course: “Everyone else is allowed!”.

It has been revealed that yes, and everyone else may make dubious choices—not exactly a convincing argument. Grand Theft Auto is known for violence, criminal activity, sexual content, and adult themes. Surprised? It’s the sixth iteration, folks. It’s Grand Theft Auto, not Careful Driving Simulator. Yet beyond the controversy surrounding the release, there are psychological questions worth considering:.

Watching Violence Is Not the Same as Participating in It.

In a recent development, kids aren’t just absorbing whatever’s on the screen. They interpret it and make their own sense of it. Video games add another wrinkle: instead of only watching a character act aggressively, players make choices and see what follows. Albert Bandura’s (2001) social cognitive theory helps us understand this. Children learn through observation, and behaviors can be rewarded or produce desirable outcomes. However, learning about a behavior is not the same as performing it. A teen who successfully steals a virtual car isn’t necessarily planning to steal the neighbor’s Honda.

According to recent reports, researchers still argue about how violent games relate to aggression. Some studies have found links with aggressive thoughts or behavior (Anderson and colleagues, 2010); others found no meaningful link between playing violent games and adolescent aggression (Przybylski and Weinstein, 2019). The answer isn’t as simple as violent game in, violent kid out. Your teenager’s brain is not one-size-fits-all. Two teens the same age can react differently to the same game. One might see the violence as exaggerated satire; another might find it upsetting or miss the point. Maturity, past experiences, and individual sensitivities matter, and age alone doesn’t tell us how a child will respond.

Age-rating systems are a helpful starting point, but the ratings don’t explain how parents can understand developmental differences. Adults can consider a child’s maturity, awareness of specific content, and ability to distinguish fictional scenarios from real-world behavior. Understanding that something is fictional doesn’t mean a child is emotionally prepared for it.

For teens, video games aren’t necessarily just games. They’re opportunities for social connection, common experiences, and participation in peer culture. Belonging is especially vital during adolescence. Being excluded from something friends are discussing or playing can feel like being excluded from the group itself.

Sources indicate that that doesn’t mean parents should say yes to help their child fit in. But a teen’s interest in the new Grand Theft Auto may be less about virtual crime than about joining a conversation their friends are having. Ask what appeals to them: the story, exploring the world, the humor, or that everyone’s talking about it? Hear them out. This may be better than shutting the conversation down with an automatic no. What does the game teach? Rather than focusing on the violence, consider: What aggressive behavior is rewarded, how are consequences portrayed, how is satire used to criticize society, and would younger players take it literally?

Sources indicate that talk it through with your kids. They’re still learning how to make sense of complicated stories, relationships, and questions about right and wrong. And humor adds a further layer. Grand Theft Auto is known for exaggerated social commentary and dark humor. Still, understanding satire requires distinguishing between what is depicted and what is being criticized.

A younger player may recognize that a character is behaving badly without understanding the larger social commentary. Even when adolescents recognize satire, that doesn’t automatically mean every aspect of the content is appropriate for them.

Before spending money on the latest installment of virtual criminal behavior, parents might want to do a little research:.

Conversations about how the game portrays violence, relationships, and consequences can help kids think critically about what they’re seeing.

It has been revealed that parental controls can manage access, purchases, and playtime. Remember, restricting a game at home doesn’t necessarily prevent children from encountering it through friends, YouTube, or social media. We were once kids too. Don’t tell me that while reading this, you didn't remember something you did outside your home that your parents still don’t know about.

Is Grand Theft Auto VI Worth It?

Industry observers note that adults who enjoy open-world narratives may believe it is worth it. When a 12-year-old states everyone already has it, we might have to reconsider. Recognize how gaming matters to your teen without buying the game. Their interest deserves a conversation; your boundaries continue to matter. We don’t need another moral panic about video games. However, we also don’t need to pretend that all media experiences are appropriate for every child. Sometimes the most responsible parenting decision is to say yes. Sometimes it’s to say no. And sometimes it’s to say, “Let’s find out a little more about this game before I spend my hard-earned money on your virtual crime spree.”.

After all, just because a game allows you to steal a car doesn’t mean parents should abandon the driver’s seat.

#178588. Tech Report: In the Berkshires, an Intensely Yellow Kitchen Is Anything but Mellow in This Lakeside Cottage
